chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from some of his companions, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I was with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام at the funeral of a man from our companions. When they had buried him, he عليه السلام went to his grave, cast upon it three handfuls of soil from the side near his head with both his hands, then spread his palm over the grave,

then he said: “O Allah, keep the earth away from his sides, raise his soul up to You, grant him meeting with pleasure from You, and settle in his grave such mercy from You as will make him independent of the mercy of anyone besides You.”

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah, a direct invocation in supplication
key_terms.جِنَازَةِ: the funeral procession or funeral of the deceased
key_terms.رَحْمَتِكَ: Your mercy, sought for the deceased in the grave
key_terms.رُوحَهُ: his soul, prayed to be raised to Allah
key_terms.رِضْوَانًا: divine good pleasure and acceptance from Allah
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave, the place of burial

ai.seo_question: What duʿa did Imām Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام recite at the grave after burial?
ai.summary: This hadith describes an act performed by Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام after a burial and records the supplication he recited for the deceased. It highlights praying for divine mercy, ease in the grave, and Allah’s good pleasure for the dead.
